properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 5 at 9:29AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall that has occurred upstream will maintain river levels
within Moderate flood stage through early next week as water works
north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 3.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Thursday was 3.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain nearly steady above
flood stage at 3.3 feet late this week with a slow rise this
weekend reaching 3.5 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.description:
FFWMRX

The National Weather Service in Morristown has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Polk County in east Tennessee...

* Until 1100 AM EST.

* At 857 AM EST, Local law enforcement reported widespread
catastrophic flash flooding was still ongoing with numerous
businesses and homes under several feet of water.

FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY for Copperhill. This is a PARTICULARLY
DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER GROUND NOW!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER
GROUND NOW! Life threatening flash flooding of low water
crossings, small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ducktown and Copperhill.
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now! This is an extremely dangerous and
life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are
fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 5 at 5:47AM MST until November 5 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Navajo County in north central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 800 PM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 544 AM MST, a river gauge on the Little Colorado River at
Winslow had dropped below action stage. Water levels are forecast
to continue to fall through today, however flooding will remain a
threat downstream at Birdsprings through this evening.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 5:00am MST the stage was 16.56 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Leupp, Birdsprings, Sunrise and Homolovi Ruins State Park.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

* WHEN...From Thursday evening through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach

properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...North Central Socorro County in central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...River or stream flows are elevated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 500 PM MST, emergency management reported flooding in the
advisory area from rising river levels along the Rio Puerco. This
will cause arroyo and small stream flooding. Rapid river rises
will cause minor flooding in the advisory area.
- For Rio Puerco at Bernardo:
At 4:00pm the stage was 14.08 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.5 feet.
- For Rio Grande at San Acacia:
At 4:45pm the stage was 14.83 feet.
Flood Stage is 23.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 AM MST THURSDAY

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 4 at 3:29PM PST until November 5 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 8 to 11 ft with dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Additional High Surf Advisories and Coastal
Flood Advisories may be needed in the near future.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Alamosa, CO; Conejos, CO; Costilla, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 4 at 3:44PM MST until November 5 at 3:45PM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
Flooding continues along the Conejos and San Antonio Rivers in
eastern Conejos County.

* WHAT...Flooding continues along the Conejos River and San Antonio
River towards their confluence with the Rio Grande, downstream of
Alamosa.

* WHERE...Northeastern Conejos County in south central Colorado...
West Central Costilla County in south central Colorado...
South Central Alamosa County in southeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 345 PM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Conejos River and San Antonio River,
along with other low-lying and flood-prone locations, continues in
eastern Conejos County. Inundation of low-lying areas near and
downstream of the confluence with the Rio Grande is also expected.
Some roads remain closed due to flooding. Expect many areas of slow
moving or standing water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 343 PM MST, Flooding has been ongoing in the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Manassa, Sanford and Lasauses.
- http://www.water.noaa.gov
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 3 at 8:20AM MST until November 5 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues along the
San Juan River from near Bluff to the terminus at Lake Powell.

* WHERE...Southwestern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...River levels continue to rise due to excess runoff from
Sunday's rainfall. Expect high water levels and the River exceeding
its banks, inundating low-lying areas along the San Juan River. A
prolonged period of high water is forecast, with a crest near 23.5
ft Thursday morning. It will take several hours for all the water
from these storms to work through local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 813 AM MST, stream gauge reports indicates the observed stage
on the San Juan River at Bluff has exceeded flood stage and is at
23.7 feet. Timing of additional crests is subject to change as
more details become available. Please continue to monitor the
forecast and updated  warnings.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
the San Juan River from Bluff to the terminus at Lake Powell.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 515 PM MST THURSDAY

properties.areaDesc: Alamosa, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 3:29PM MST until November 6 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Colorado...

Rio Grande At Alamosa affecting Alamosa County.

.Minor flooding along the Rio Grande through Alamosa is expected due
to upstream flooding occurring in the vicinity of Monte Vista.

For the Rio Grande...including Alamosa...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Alamosa.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon to late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor flooding. Minor agricultural flooding
in low lying areas along the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM MST Monday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Wednesday afternoon to a crest of 9.6 feet late Wednesday
evening. It will then fall below flood stage early Thursday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.water.noaa.gov
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

This warning will be in effect until the river falls below its flood
stage.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1100 AM MST.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT FROM WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON TO LATE THURSDAY NIGHT... ...REPLACES RIVER FLOOD WATCH

properties.areaDesc: Montezuma, CO; San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 12:31PM MST until November 5 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the San Juan River caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...along the San Juan River from the Four Corners through
Mexican Hat, UT. This includes Bluff, Montezuma Creek and Aneth.

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...River levels continue to rise due to excess runoff from
Sunday's rainfall. Expect high water levels and the River exceeding
its banks, inundating low-lying areas along the San Juan River. A
prolonged period of high water is forecast, with a crest near 23.5
ft Thursday morning. It will take several hours for all the water
from these storms to work through local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1222 PM MST, stream gauge reports upstream and impacts of
flooding have been reported along the San Juan River near
Farmington, NM. Expect flood waters to reach the Four Corners
Wednesday evening and the town of Bluff early Thursday morning.
Timing of crest is subject to change as more details become
available. Please continue to monitor the forecast and updated
warnings.
- At 11:30 AM MST Monday the stage was 20.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 22 feet late this evening with
a secondary crest near 23.5 feet expected near Bluff early
Thursday morning. It will then fall below flood stage Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Bluff, Montezuma Creek, and Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT UNTIL 515 PM MST THURSDAY
